findings.location: Positive owned CodeGraph state binding, DisposeOwnedStateAsync signature and ownership verifier; plan.md ID-I07, ID-S06 and ID-T06
findings.affected_requirement: spec FR-012 and SC-007; O-NFR01; Constitution I and V
findings.evidence: The plan requires a fresh exact source-approval and CodeGraph-purpose check before deleting the owned .codegraph entry, including after the original lease is revoked. The specified DisposeOwnedStateAsync accepts only PreparedCodeGraphWorkspaceOwnership and cancellation; its coordinator constructor accepts only a workspace-ownership verifier described as checking the owner record. Neither callable input nor dependency supplies the current source and tool-purpose verifiers used by the lease. Implementing the documented disposal check would therefore require an undisclosed authority seam, while omitting it would allow deletion under stale or unavailable source/tool authority.
findings.correction_outcome: Specify how disposition obtains and verifies the current exact source approval, CodeGraph tool purpose, workspace owner and root/entry identity without reusing a revoked lease. Align the callable contract, failure/quarantine behavior and ID-T06 controlled verification with that source of authority.

raw_result.summary: Plan-only REVISE. Prior PATH trust, task launch-order, partial-open ownership and runtime-settings findings remain resolved. The raw protocol-string boundary addresses the device-path testability issue, and the in-place state plan preserves Story 18.1's public read contract and separate JDT state. One plan-owned blocker remains: disposition cannot perform fresh source/tool authorization through its stated interface. Native CodeGraph child confinement, ordinary-reader repair and real JDT qualification remain later dependencies; controlled tests do not satisfy them. No tasks or implementation were reviewed.
